what_it_does: Quantum computers represent real-world physical systems using qubits (quantum bits), but mapping fermionic systems (systems of electrons) to qubits requires converting fermionic operators into qubit operators—a transformation that produces complex expressions called Hamiltonians. The more complex the expression, the more quantum gates are needed, and quantum gates are expensive and noisy. This paper presents HATT (Hamiltonian Adaptive Ternary Tree), which tailors the fermionic-to-qubit mapping to the specific problem structure rather than using generic mappings. By analyzing the structure of each problem's Hamiltonian and constructing a custom ternary tree mapping, HATT reduces the complexity of quantum circuits while maintaining correctness, and drops computational overhead from O(N^4) to O(N^3) where N is the problem size.
